repositories.description: The Neuroscience Information Framework is a dynamic inventory of Web-based neuroscience resources: data, materials, and tools accessible via any computer connected to the Internet. An initiative of the NIH Blueprint for Neuroscience Research, NIF advances neuroscience research by enabling discovery and access to public research data and tools worldwide through an open source, networked environment.
repositories.subject_area: Behavioral and social sciences, Imaging, Neuroscience, Sequence biology

repositories.name: OpenPain
repositories.description: The OpenPain includes a data repository of pain and brain MRI data that are collected in subjects undergoing total knee arthroplasty (TKA) and a brain imaging-based prognostic algorism (software development) to prospectively predict outcomes following total knee replacement.

repositories.name: AphasiaBank
repositories.description: AphasiaBank is a shared database of multimedia interactions for the study of communication in aphasia. Access to the data in AphasiaBank is password protected and restricted to members of the AphasiaBank consortium group.
repositories.subject_area: Behavioral and social sciences, Clinical research

repositories.name: FluencyBank
repositories.description: FluencyBank is a shared database for the study of fluency development. Participants include typically-developing monolingual and bilingual children, children and adults who stutter (C/AWS) or who clutter (C/AWC), and second language learners.
repositories.subject_area: Behavioral and social sciences, Clinical research, Neuroscience

repositories.name: gEAR
repositories.description: gEAR portal is a community driven, multi-omic data exploration portal for Gene Expression Analysis Resource (gEAR) studies related to the cochlea

repositories.name: FaceBase
repositories.description: FaceBase serves as a "one stop shop" for research in dental, oral, craniofacial, inner ear (DOCIE), and associated systemic conditions spanning the full translational spectrum. The data repository is funded by NIDCR, NIDCD, and OD, housing multidimensional, research laboratory, and real-world data (RWD) in support of advancing research. The repository continually accommodates appropriate public data sharing, spotlighting AI-ready molecular, genetic, multiomic, imaging, and real-world data, offering data processing, visualization, and analysis tools, and implementing state-of-the-art computational techniques. FaceBase constantly works to improve its interoperability to support research in DOCIE and other biologically and anatomically relevant health domains

repositories.name: Candida Genome Database
repositories.description: The Candida Genome Database (CGD), a resource for genomic sequence data and gene and protein information for Candida albicans and related species. The CGD provides online access to genomic sequence data and manually curated functional information about genes and proteins of the human pathogen Candida albicans and related species. C. albicans is the best studied of the human fungal pathogens. It is a common commensal organism of healthy individuals but can cause debilitating mucosal infections and life-threatening systemic infections, especially in immunocompromised patients. C. albicans also serves as a model organism for the study of other fungal pathogens.

repositories.name: Human Oral Microbiome Database (HOMD)
repositories.description: The HOMD is a NIDCR supported comprehensive database of the microbiota within the human mouth and aerodigestive tract. HOMD provides provisional naming schemes for unnamed taxa, links to sequence data with phenotypic, phylogenetic, clinical and bibliographic information, and easy to use tools for viewing genome information.

repositories.name: Human Salivary Proteome
repositories.description: The Human Salivary Proteome Wiki is a a NIDCR-funded collaborative, community-based Web portal to more than 1,000 unique human saliva proteins identified by high-throughput proteomic technologies. The wiki knowledgebase is available for the research community and the public to harness the knowledge in the data and to further enhance the value of the proteome through addition of their own data. Researchers are welcome to browse datasets, analyse salivary protein sequences, expressions and signatures; add their own data to the growing knowledgebase; annotate the proteins; or just explore the site.
repositories.subject_area: Clinical research, Computational biology, Sequence biology

repositories.name: NIDA Data Share
repositories.description: The NIDA Data Share web site is an electronic environment that allows data from completed clinical trials to be distributed to investigators and the public in order to promote new research, encourage further analyses, and disseminate information to the community. Secondary analyses produced from data sharing multiply the scientific contribution of the original research. NIH expects and supports the timely release and sharing of final research data from NIH-supported studies for use by other researchers to expedite the translation of research results into knowledge, products and procedures to improve human health.
repositories.subject_area: Behavioral and social sciences, Clinical research, Other

repositories.name: NIDDK-Central Repository Resources for Research (NIDDK-CR R4R)
repositories.description: NIDDK Central Repository - Resources for Research (NIDDK-CR R4R) facilitates sharing of data, biospecimens, and other resources generated from studies supported by NIDDK and within NIDDK's mission by making these resources available for request to the broader scientific and research community.
repositories.subject_area: Clinical research, Computational biology, Imaging, Other, Real-World Data

repositories.name: United States Renal Data System (USRDS)
repositories.description: The United States Renal Data System (USRDS) is a national data system that collects, analyzes, and distributes information about chronic kidney disease (CKD) and end-stage renal disease (ESRD) in the United States. The USRDS is funded directly by the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK). USRDS staff collaborate with members of Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN), and the ESRD networks, sharing datasets and working to improve the accuracy of ESRD patient information.

repositories.name: Accelerating Medicines Partnership in Common Metabolic Diseases Knowledge Portal (AMP-CMDKP)
repositories.description: The Common Metabolic Diseases Knowledge Portal (CMDKP) aggregates and analyzes genetic association results, epigenomic annotations, and results of computational prediction methods to provide data, visualizations, and tools in an open-access portal. The aim of the CMDKP is to facilitate research on the molecular basis of complex diseases, including type 1 and type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, and sleep disorders.

repositories.name: Accelerating Medicines Partnership in Type 2 Diabetes Knowledge Portal (AMP-T2D)
repositories.description: The T2D Knowledge Portal enables browsing, searching, and analysis of human genetic information linked to type 2 diabetes and related traits, while protecting the integrity and confidentiality of the underlying data.

repositories.name: Chemical Effects in Biological Systems (CEBS)
repositories.description: The CEBS database houses data of interest to environmental health scientists. CEBS is a public resource, and has received depositions of data from academic, industrial, and governmental laboratories. Data in CEBS are housed in a relational database designed to display data in the context of biology and study design, and permit data integration for cross-study analysis, knowledge generation and novel meta-analysis.

repositories.name: Exposome Correlation and Interpretation Database (ECID)
repositories.description: ECID is a biomedical knowledgebase of curated inter-chemical correlations from the core chemical datasets in exposomics. These datasets are prioritized from human biomonitoring studies using targeted and untargeted assays. ECID has applications in characterizing and understanding the effects of exposome chemicals on the human health.

repositories.name: GeoSpace
repositories.description: GeoSpace is a NIEHS funded biomedical knowledgebase to provide a curated collection of geospatial datasets and associated information. It enables, data discoverability, data harmonization and data re-uses of GeoSpatial datasets in the USA.

repositories.name: Human Health Exposure Analysis Resource (HHEAR) Data Repository
repositories.description: Human Health Exposure Analysis Resource (HHEAR) Data Center provides a data repository for storing epidemiologic and biomarker data for CHEAR and HHEAR research studies to improve our knowledge of the comprehensive effects of environmental exposures on human health throughout the life course. Registered users will have access to publicly available deidentified datasets. In addition, there is a publicly accessible HHEAR ontology that provides a common vocabulary with unambiguous definitions of concepts and variables across studies to allow for pooling of studies.

repositories.name: Integrated Chemical Environment (ICE)
repositories.description: Successful computational toxicology projects depend on high-quality data that are freely available and formatted for use in computational workflows. The Integrated Chemical Environment (ICE) addresses the data needs frequently expressed by NICEATM stakeholders. Launched in March 2017, ICE provides curated data from NICEATM, its partners, and other resources, as well as tools to facilitate the safety assessment of chemicals.

repositories.name: Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD)
repositories.description: CTD is a robust, publicly available database that aims to advance understanding about how environmental exposures affect human health. It provides manually curated information about chemical'gene/protein interactions, chemical'disease and gene'disease relationships. These data are integrated with functional and pathway data to aid in development of hypotheses about the mechanisms underlying environmentally influenced diseases.

repositories.name: Reasoning Over Biomedical Objects linked in Knowledge Oriented Pathways (ROBOKOP)
repositories.description: ROBOKOP is an open-source, modular, biomedical knowledge graph'based system that includes the ROBOKOP biomedical knowledge graph, a user interface, and a variety of supporting resources, including tools and services to support deep exploration of the ROBOKOP KG and each of its underlying primary knowledge sources.

repositories.name: Binding Database (BindingDB)
repositories.description: BindingDB is a public, web-accessible database of measured binding affinities, focusing chiefly on the interactions of proteins considered to be candidate drug-targets with ligands that are small, drug-like molecules. BindingDB supports medicinal chemistry and drug discovery via literature awareness and development of structure-activity relations (SAR and QSAR); validation of computational chemistry and molecular modeling approaches such as docking, scoring and free energy methods; chemical biology and chemical genomics; and basic studies of the physical chemistry of molecular recognition. BindingDB also includes a small collection of host-guest binding data of interest to chemists studying supramolecular systems.

repositories.name: Biological Magnetic Resonance Data Bank (BMRB)
repositories.description: BMRB collects, annotates, archives, and disseminates (worldwide in the public domain) the important spectral and quantitative data derived from NMR spectroscopic investigations of biologically relevant molecules.

repositories.name: BioPortal
repositories.description: BioPortal is the world's most comprehensive, integrated knowledgebase of biomedical ontologies and controlled terminologies. BioPortal enables users to navigate, visualize, and leverage both individual ontologies and the collective knowledge suggested by its entire knowledgebase of more than 800 ontologies. It provides specialized tools that employ novel layouts and animation to offer cognitive support to users trying to understand the complexities of large ontologies within the confines of the two dimensions offered by a Web browser.

repositories.name: DOCKGROUND
repositories.description: Adequate computational techniques for modeling of protein interactions are important because of the growing number of known protein structures. The Dockground project is designed to provide resources for the development of such techniques and increase our knowledge of protein interactions. Dockground data sets are regularly updated and annotated.

repositories.name: EcoCyc
repositories.description: The EcoCyc database describes the genome, metabolic pathways, and regulatory network of E. coli K-12 substr. MG1655. The long-term goal of the project is to describe the molecular catalog of the E. coli cell, as well as the functions of each of its molecular parts, to facilitate a system-level understanding of E. coli. EcoCyc is an electronic reference source for E. coli biologists, and for biologists who work with related microorganisms.

repositories.name: GlyGen
repositories.description: GlyGen is an international project funded by The National Institutes of Health (NIH) and The National Institute of General Medical Sciences (NIGMS) to facilitate glycoscience research by integrating diverse kinds of information related to glycoscience, including glycomics, genomics, proteomics (including glycoproteomics), cell biology, developmental biology and biochemistry.GlyGen retrieves information from multiple international data sources and integrates and harmonizes this data into a single resource. GlyGen allows for exploring this data by performing unique searches that cannot be executed in any of the existing databases alone. Information is provided in user friendly graphical web interfaces as well as machine-readable APIs.

repositories.name: Nucleic Acid Knowledge Base (NAKB)
repositories.description: The Nucleic Acid Knowledge Base (NAKB), modern successor to the Nucleic Acid Database (NDB) Project, archives and distributes structural information about nucleic acids.

repositories.name: PeptideAtlas
repositories.description: PeptideAtlas is a multi-organism, publicly accessible compendium of peptides identified in a large set of tandem mass spectrometry proteomics experiments. Mass spectrometer output files are collected for human, mouse, yeast, and several other organisms, and searched using the latest search engines and protein sequences. All results of sequence and spectral library searching are subsequently processed through the Trans Proteomic Pipeline to derive a probability of correct identification for all results in a uniform manner to insure a high-quality database, along with false discovery rates at the whole atlas level. Results may be queried and browsed at the PeptideAtlas web site. The raw data, search results, and full builds can also be downloaded for other uses.

repositories.name: Redfly
repositories.description: REDfly (Regulatory Element Database for Fly) is a curated FAIR-compliant knowledgebase that extracts, accumulates, organizes, annotates, and links the growing body of information on insect transcriptional cis-regulatory sequences. REDfly focuses on experimentally verified cis-regulatory modules (CRMs) and transcription factor binding sites and their DNA sequences, associated genes, the expression patterns they direct. REDfly is an important platform for supporting hypothesis-driven empirical and computational research and has contributed to studies in multiple areas including CRM biology, CRM discovery, regulatory networks, interpretation of genomic datasets, and evolution.

repositories.name: Research Resource Identification (RRID)
repositories.description: The RRID index is a list of key biological reagents and resources aggregated from the most authoritative data sources for each resource type. Each of the records is also available from that data source.

repositories.name: Virtual Nanostructure Simulation (VINAS) Web Portal
repositories.description: Virtual Nanomaterial Simulation Professional (ViNAS-Pro) is a data-driven nanoinformatics platform. It comprises six core components that enable data profiling, data preprocessing and visualization, machine learning (ML) modeling, virtual nanomaterials (NMs) prediction, as well as nanostructure and nanodescriptor calculation.

repositories.name: National Clinical Cohort Collaborative (N3C)
repositories.description: The N3C Data Enclave is a secure platform through which the harmonized clinical data provided by our contributing members is stored. The data itself can only be accessed through a secure cloud portal hosted by NCATS and cannot be downloaded or removed. N3C invites you to begin your journey with the Enclave and join the collaborative efforts of our partners to better understand and address the most pressing COVID-19 clinical question

repositories.name: Allen Brain Cell (ABC) Atlas (aka Adult whole brain cell atlas in human and NHP)
repositories.description: The Allen Brain Cell (ABC) Atlas provides a platform for visualizing multimodal single cell data across the mammalian brain and aims to empower researchers to explore and analyze multiple whole-brain datasets simultaneously.

repositories.name: AMP Schizophrenia (SCZ)
repositories.description: The AMP Schizophrenia (SCZ) program was launched in 2020 to address the critical need for more effective treatments for people with schizophrenia and related mental health conditions.
repositories.subject_area: Behavioral and social sciences, Clinical research, Imaging, Real-World Data

repositories.name: Brain Analysis Library of Spatial maps and Atlases (BALSA)
repositories.description: Brain Analysis Library of Spatial Maps and Atlases (BALSA)

repositories.name: Brain Image Library
repositories.description: The Brain Image Library (BIL) is a national public resource enabling researchers to deposit, analyze, mine, share and interact with large brain image datasets.

repositories.name: BRAIN Initiative - Cell Atlas Network (BICAN)
repositories.description: The BRAIN Initiative' Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) is a collaborative effort between neuroscientists, computational biologists and software engineers to create a comprehensive atlas of the human brain. Supported by the U.S. BRAIN Initiative, we are dedicated to advancing our knowledge of the brain by gathering and sharing new data that allows us to develop the 'parts list' of the brain, detailing the vast array of neurons and non-neuronal cells in the human brain. The BICAN continues the work of the BICCN consortium.

repositories.name: Distributed Archives for Neurophysiology Data Integration (The DANDI Archive)
repositories.description: The BRAIN Initiative archive for publishing and sharing neurophysiology data including electrophysiology, optophysiology, and behavioral time-series, and images from immunostaining experiments.
repositories.subject_area: Behavioral and social sciences, Imaging, Neuroscience

repositories.name: Ecosystem for Multi-modal Brain-behavior Experimentation and Research (EMBER)
repositories.description: EMBER (Ecosystem for Multi-modal Brain-behavior Experimentation and Research) is the BRAIN Initiative data archive for multi-modal neurophysiological and behavioral data, supporting the Brain Behavior Quantification and Synchronization (BBQS) Program.
repositories.subject_area: Clinical research, Computational biology, Neuroscience, Real-World Data

repositories.name: Neuroelectromagnetic Data Archive and Tools Resource (NEMAR)
repositories.description: NEMAR, the NeuroElectroMagnetic data Archive and tools Resource, is an NIMH BRAIN Initiative funded data, tools, and compute resource for (EEG, MEG, and iEEG) data shared publicly through the (all modalities) OpenNeuro archive of human neuroimaging data

repositories.name: Neuroscience Multi-omic Archive (NeMO)
repositories.description: The Neuroscience Multi-omic Archive (NeMO Archive) is a data repository specifically focused on the storage and dissemination of omic data generated from the BRAIN Initiative and related brain research projects.

repositories.name: NeuroVault and NeuroSynth
repositories.description: Neurosynth is a platform for large-scale, automated synthesis of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data. NeuroVault is a public repository of unthresholded statistical maps, parcellations, and atlases of the brain.

repositories.name: National Neighborhood Data Archive (NaNDA)
repositories.description: The National Neighborhood Data Archive (NaNDA) is a publicly available data archive containing contextual measures for locations across the United States. NaNDA offers theoretically derived, spatially referenced, nationwide measures of the physical and social environment. Each NaNDA dataset represents a set of measures on a single topic of interest. Examples of topics to be found in NaNDA (now or in the future) include socioeconomic disadvantage and affluence, walkability, crime, land use, recreational centers, libraries, fast food, climate, healthcare, housing, public transit, and more.

repositories.name: Brain Observatory Storage Service & Database (BossDB)
repositories.description: BossDB is a volumetric database for 3D and 4D neuroscience data.

repositories.name: Data Archive for the BRAIN Initiative (DABI)
repositories.description: Building on decades of experience creating widely-used, large-scale informatics solutions in the neurosciences, in 2018, the team behind DABI launched a new archive to ingest, aggregate, store, visualize, and disseminate human invasive neurophysiology data. DABI repository, which also houses synchronized behavioral, imaging, demographic, and other vital data, is specifically designed to help BRAIN Initiative researchers organize and analyze their data while fulfilling data-sharing directives from federal agencies and their respective institutions.
repositories.subject_area: Behavioral and social sciences, Imaging, Neuroscience

repositories.name: OpenNeuro
repositories.description: A free and open platform for validating and sharing BIDS-compliant MRI, PET, MEG, EEG, and iEEG data

repositories.name: SCHARE (NIMHD)
repositories.description: SCHARE is a cloud-based platform for health research designed to leverage population science, place-based, and behavioral Big Data and cloud computing tools to foster a paradigm shift in population health research to generate innovative whole-person health discoveries using AI, advance the use of transparency and sophisticated inquiry to develop innovative strategies and differing perspectives to reduce AI errors, upskill novice untrained users in data science through cloud computing skills training, cross-discipline mentoring, and multi-career'level collaborating on research, provide a data science cloud computing resource for community colleges and low- resource institutions and organizations, and offer a project data repository centered on core common data elements for enhanced data interoperability and compliance with NIH Data Management and Sharing Policy.
repositories.subject_area: Behavioral and social sciences, Clinical research

repositories.name: Accelerating Medicine Partnership in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (AMP-ALS), ALS Knowledge Portal
repositories.description: The AMP ALS Program is a collaborative effort that unites resources and expertise from the National Institutes of Health (NIH), academia, life science companies, foundations, patient-focused organizations, and research nonprofits. Its goal is to address the significant challenges in diagnosing, understanding, and treating amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a progressive and fatal neurological disease. AMP ALS is building the largest data resource for ALS research to accelerate the discovery of biomarkers and clinical outcome assessments, enabling earlier diagnosis and faster development of effective treatments.
repositories.subject_area: Clinical research, Computational biology, Neuroscience, Other, Sequence biology

repositories.name: NINDS Human Cell and Data Repository (NHCDR)
repositories.description: The NINDS Human Cell and Data Repository (NHCDR) provides access to fibroblast and/or induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines for a number neurological disorders within the NINDS mission as well as healthy controls. NHCDR also supports access to unique iPSC collections from NeuroLINCS, PDBP, LEFFTDS and Target ALS with associated metadata. A GMP-grade iPSC line and corresponding research grade iPSC line are also available through the NHCDR.

repositories.name: Parkinson's Disease Biomarker Program
repositories.description: The NINDS Parkinsons Disease (PD) Biomarkers Program Data Management Resource (PDBP DMR) enables web-based data entry for clinical studies supporting PD biomarker development, as well as broad data sharing of longitudinal neuroimaging, clinical, genetic, and biospecimen data across the entire PD research community. The PDBP DMR coordinates information and access to PD biospecimens distributed through the NINDS BioSEND and Human Cell and Data repositories.
repositories.subject_area: Behavioral and social sciences, Clinical research, Imaging, Neuroscience, Sequence biology

repositories.name: Imaging Repository for the Cerebrovascular Disease Knowledge Portal (iCDKP)
repositories.description: The Imaging Cerebrovascular Disease Knowledge Portal (iCDKP) is a repository that provides researchers with open access to MRI and CT images for analysis. This unprecedented access to imaging data enables a comprehensive understanding of the brain's response to stroke, including quantifying tissue involvement, characterizing stroke mechanism, infarct size and location, and more.

repositories.name: Open Data Commons - Traumatic Brain Injury (ODC-TBI)
repositories.description: The Open Data Commons - Traumatic Brain Injury (ODC-TBI) is a dedicated data sharing portal and repository for pre-clinical TBI research. TBI data can be shared with certain users in a protected space and when ready, TBI data can be shared with the public through a DOI. ODC-TBI complies with the FAIR data principles to ensure that TBI data is Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable while promoting transparency, rigor and reproducibility in pre-clinical TBI research. ODC-TBI is providing the data sharing platform for the new interagency PREClinical Interagency reSearch resourcE for TBI (PRECISE-TBI)

repositories.name: Open Data Commons for Spinal Cord Injury
repositories.description: The Open Data Commons for Spinal Cord Injury (ODC-SCI.org), is a community-based, dedicated data sharing portal and repository for the field of SCI where researchers can share data with colleagues in a protected space and publish data to the public with a DOI. The ODC-SCI involves a curation process and complies with the FAIR data principles to ensure that SCI data is Findable, Accessible, Interoperable and Reusable. Releasing a DOI thus requires the submission of metadata and a data dictionary.

repositories.name: ClinicalTrials.gov
repositories.description: ClinicalTrials.gov is a registry and results database of privately and publicly funded clinical studies conducted around the world. Structured study information is submitted by the sponsor or investigator responsible for the research, either voluntarily or to meet legal or policy requirements.

repositories.name: ClinVar
repositories.description: ClinVar is a public archive of submitted reports about the relationships between human genomic variations and inherited diseases, cancer, and drug responses, with supporting evidence.

repositories.name: Conserved Domains Database (CDD)
repositories.description: The Conserved Domain Database is a resource for the annotation of functional units in proteins. Its collection of domain models includes a set curated by NCBI, which utilizes 3D structure to provide insights into sequence/structure/function relationships.

repositories.name: Database for Genotypes and Phenotypes (dbGaP)
repositories.description: The database of Genotypes and Phenotypes (dbGaP) archives and provides controlled access, for NIH approved users, to data from studies that have investigated the interaction of genotype and phenotype in humans.
repositories.subject_area: Behavioral and social sciences, Clinical research, Computational biology, Imaging, Sequence biology

repositories.name: Database of human genomic Structural Variation (dbVar)
repositories.description: dbVar is NCBI's database of human genomic Structural Variation, comprised of large variants >50 bp, including insertions, deletions, duplications, inversions, mobile elements, translocations, and complex variants
repositories.subject_area: Clinical research, Computational biology, Sequence biology

repositories.name: GenBank
repositories.description: GenBank is the NIH genetic sequence database, an annotated collection of publicly available DNA sequences. GenBank captures, preserves, and presents comprehensive nucleotide sequence information and annotations from around the world and connects these data, where applicable, to associated scientific publications and the biological specimens from which the data were derived.

repositories.name: Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO)
repositories.description: GEO is a functional genomics data repository that archives and distributes open-access array- and sequence-based genomic datasets including gene expression and epigenomics.

repositories.name: Mass Spectrometry Interactive Virtual Environment (MassIVE)
repositories.description: MassIVE is a community resource for Computational Mass Spectrometry to promote the global, free exchange of mass spectrometry data.

repositories.name: National Database of Antimicrobial Resisant Organisms (NDARO)
repositories.description: The National Database of Antibiotic Resistant Organisms is a collaborative, cross-agency, centralized hub for researchers to access data on antimicrobial resistance (AMR), including AMR genes and genetic and antibiotic susceptibility data, to facilitate real-time surveillance of pathogenic organisms.

repositories.name: NCBI Datasets: Gene, Genome, Assembly, Orthologs, and Taxonomy Database
repositories.description: NCBI Datasets is both a knowledge base and an access point for data. It provides descriptive information about Genes, Genomes, Orthologs, and Taxonomic classification, as well as interfaces to download gene, ortholog, and genomic data and metadata.

repositories.name: NIH Genetic Testing Registry (GTR)
repositories.description: The Genetic Testing Registry provides information about genetic and genomic tests available for clinical and research use, along with details about the laboratories that offer the tests. The registry includes molecular, biochemical and cytogenetic human genetic tests, as well as serologic and molecular microbe tests.

repositories.name: Pathogen Detection
repositories.description: NCBI Pathogen Detection integrates bacterial and fungal pathogen genomic sequences from numerous ongoing surveillance and research efforts whose sources include food, environmental sources such as water or production facilities, and patient samples. Foodborne, hospital-acquired, and other clinically infectious pathogens are included.

repositories.name: Protein Family Models
repositories.description: Protein Family Models is a collection of models representing homologous proteins with a common function. It includes conserved domain architectures, hidden Markov models, and BlastRules that represent families found in prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

repositories.name: PubChem
repositories.description: PubChem is the world's largest collection of freely accessible information on chemical substances, including chemical names, biological activities, physical properties, safety and toxicity information, patents, and literature citations. Chemicals can be searched by name, molecular formula, structure, and other identifiers.

repositories.name: Reference Sequences (RefSeq)
repositories.description: RefSeq is a database of integrated, non-redundant, well-annotated references sequences, including genomic DNA, transcripts, and proteins. RefSeq genomes are compies of selected genomes available in GenBank, while RefSeq transcript and proteins records are generated through computation, manual curation, and other methods.

repositories.name: Sequence Read Archive (SRA)
repositories.description: The Sequence Read Archive (SRA) is the largest publicly available repository of high throughput sequencing data. It accepts data from all branches of life as well as metagenomic and environmental surveys. The data are available through multiple cloud providers and NCBI servers.

repositories.name: Single Nucleotide Polymorphism Database (dbSNP)
repositories.description: The dbSNP repository contains human single nucleotide variations, microsatellites, and small-scale insertions and deletions along with information about publications, population frequency, molecular consequence, and genomic and RefSeq mapping information. In addition to single nucleotide alterations that are common enough in a population to be referred to as polymorphic, dbSNP also includes rare variants, such as those with clinical assertions in NCBI's ClinVar repository.
repositories.subject_area: Clinical research, Computational biology, Other, Sequence biology

repositories.name: All of Us
repositories.description: All of Us is working to improve health care through research. Unlike research studies that focus on one disease or group of people, All of Us is building a diverse database that can inform thousands of studies on a variety of health conditions.

repositories.name: Biological General Repository for Interaction Datasets (BioGRID)
repositories.description: The BioGRID Open Respository of CRISPR Screens (ORCS) is a publicly accessible database of CRISPR screens compiled through comprehensive curation of all genome-wide CRISPR screen data reported in the biomedical literature.

repositories.name: Dark Kinase Knowledge Base
repositories.description: The goal of the DKK is to generate, systematize and disseminate knowledge about dark kinases, biological networks in which they function and connections to cellular phenotypes and human disease.

repositories.name: HuBMAP Data Portal
repositories.description: The focus of HuBMAP is understanding the intrinsic intra-, inter-, and extra- cellular biomolecular distribution in human tissue. HuBMAP will focus on fresh, fixed, or frozen healthy human tissue using in situ and dissociative techniques that have high-spatial resolution.The HuBMAP Data Portal aims to be an open map of the human body at the cellular level. These tools and maps are openly available, to accelerate understanding of the relationships between cell and tissue organization and function and human health.

repositories.name: INCLUDE Data Hub
repositories.description: The goal of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) INCLUDE Project is to improve the health and quality of life for people with Down syndrome (DS). INCLUDE stands for INvestigation of Co-occurring conditions across the Lifespan to Understand Down syndromE. People with Down syndrome develop certain medical conditions, like Alzheimer's disease and autoimmune conditions, more often than the general population, yet they seem to be protected from some cancers and other common co-occurring conditions. In 2018, the NIH launched the INCLUDE Project to help understand why. The INCLUDE Project aims to study the root causes of co-occurring conditions experienced by people with Down syndrome. This research will also help others without Down syndrome who are affected by the same conditions.

repositories.name: JAX Cre Repository
repositories.description: The JAX Cre Repository's aim is to provide the scientific community with a centralized, comprehensive set of well-characterized Cre Driver lines and related information resources. Available strains include Cre expressing strains, inducible Cre strains, Cre reporter strains, and loxP-flanked (floxed) strains.

repositories.name: Kids First Data Resource Center
repositories.description: The Kids First Data Resource Center (Kids First DRC) provides robust genetic and clinical data for pediatric cancer and congenital disorders. Kids First data is accessible to researchers worldwide, free of charge, to help us understand these diseases better.

repositories.name: LONI Database
repositories.description: The LONI Image Data Archive (IDA) is a user-friendly environment for archiving, searching, sharing, tracking and disseminating neuroimaging and related clinical data. The IDA is utilized for dozens of neuroimaging research projects across North America and Europe and accommodates MRI, PET, MRA, DTI and other imaging modalities.
repositories.subject_area: Behavioral and social sciences, Clinical research, Imaging, Neuroscience

repositories.name: Monarch Initiative
repositories.description: The Monarch Initiative is an integrative data and analytic platform connecting phenotypes to genotypes across species, bridging basic and applied research with semantics-based analysis. The correlation of phenotypic outcomes and disease with genetic variation and environmental factors is a core pursuit in biology and biomedicine. We have created or currently contribute to many essential bio-ontologies that together enable sophisticated and semantically integrated computational analysis across gene, genotype, variant, disease, and phenotype data. We have developed algorithms and tools that are in use by multiple communities for tasks including the identification of animal models of human disease through phenotypic similarity, phenotype-driven computational support for differential diagnostics, and translational research.

repositories.name: MoTrPAC Data Hub
repositories.description: The MoTrPAC Data Hub is the portal to access data generated by the Molecular Transducers of Physical Activity Consortium (MoTrPAC). The Data Hub allows researchers to access data from preclinical animal studies, and from the MoTrPAC clinical study. Data includes phenotypic and muti-omic data from up to 19 different animal tissues; and clinical and muti-omic data from human exercise studies
